answer_sql:
SELECT
  cc.country_name AS country,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN s.country_code = c.country_code THEN f.net_amount ELSE 0 END), 2) AS revenue_buyer_matches_shop_country,
  ROUND(SUM(f.net_amount), 2) AS revenue_all_sales_by_buyer_country,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN s.country_code = '--' THEN f.net_amount ELSE 0 END), 2) AS web_shop_revenue_in_the_gap
FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS f
JOIN contoso_served.dim_customer AS c
  ON f.customer_key = c.customer_key
JOIN contoso_served.dim_store AS s
  ON f.store_key = s.store_key
JOIN contoso_served.dim_country AS cc
  ON c.country_code = cc.country_code
GROUP BY
  1
ORDER BY
  2 DESC

sections.title: What it says its rows are

body.value: Eight rows, one per country, each saying how much money Contoso actually took — net of discount, in USD — from sales rung up at physical shops standing in that country to buyers who live in that same country, across all ten years on record, 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31. The eight add to 132,024,417.53. The important thing about this quantity: the "same country" condition did no work. Measurement showed that no buyer in this bundle has ever bought from a physical shop outside their own country, so these figures are simply each country's physical-shop revenue. WHAT IS NOT IN THEM: the web shop, 93,550 sales lines and 86,790,054.13 — 40% of all recorded revenue — which the condition removed because the web shop's country is the '--' sentinel that no customer can match. Also not included: gross revenue before discount, any currency conversion (the amounts are USD as stored), and no period was narrowed away.
